test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The average runs scored by a batsman in 23 matches is 42. In the next 10 matches, the batsman scored an average of 14 runs. Find his average runs scored (rounded off to two decimal places) in all the 33 matches.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the assumed combined average be 14 (the smaller average of the two groups).

Excess deviation for 23 matches = 23 × (42 − 14) = 23 × 28 = +644

Average excess distributed over all 33 matches = 644 ÷ 33 ≈ 19.52

Actual combined average = Assumed Average + Net Deviation = 14 + 19.52 = 33.52

**∴ The correct answer is 33.52 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 23 Matches
 Average: 42
 Total: 966

 
 10 Matches
 Average: 14

 

 Combined 33 Matches → Avg ≈ 33.52

**Given:**

Number of initial matches (n₁) = 23

Average of initial matches (A₁) = 42

Number of next matches (n₂) = 10

Average of next matches (A₂) = 14

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total runs scored in 23 matches = 23 × 42 = 966

⇒ Total runs scored in 10 matches = 10 × 14 = 140

⇒ Total runs scored in all 33 matches = 966 + 140 = 1106

⇒ Combined Average = Total runs ÷ Total matches

⇒ Combined Average = 1106 ÷ 33

⇒ Combined Average ≈ 33.5151...

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places, we get 33.52

**∴ The correct answer is 33.52 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

Used when calculating the average of two or more groups with different sample sizes. Formula: A = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Deviation Method

A simpler calculation approach where an assumed average is taken, and the net positive or negative deviations are equally shared among the entire total quantity.

Arithmetic Mean

The foundational concept of average representing the sum of all numerical values in a collection divided by the total count of those values.
